rows.exact_requirement_text:
Each ADHD server must support multiple projects while continuing to federate with
other servers. One server per project remains a valid deployment, rather than a
product restriction. This program has integrated multi-project contracts and an
initially admitted implementation. Final qualification remains open; the execution
order and acceptance gates below still govern completion. Historical single-project
results do not attest the combined architecture.

The `components/hub/multi/spec.md` contract and
[scope inventory](../protocol/scopes.json) own the replacement boundaries.
Current artifact-bound results are linked from the [project/migration proof](../../verification/multi-eventing/native-project-migration-30.json)
and [eventing/federation proof](../verification/native-eventing.json). Container,
deployment and remaining regression qualification are still in progress.

This program belongs to ADHD's hub Component, tests, tooling and guides. It does
not require a framework pin upgrade, a new model or a database replacement. The
[Kafka program](kafka-pubsub.md) supplies one Kafka service per server for project
events, optional model filters and A2A agent access; broker replication is not the
federation transport. BUILD-001's upstream publication/adoption remains separate.
Implementation proceeds in authorized local feature branches; external publication
remains separately governed.
| Entity | Identity and boundary |
| Server | One stable server ID; owns listener, durable configuration, users/authentication, server roles, model resources and peer trust. |
| Project | Stable opaque project ID distinct from a mutable display name and legacy aliases; belongs to one local server. Federated references include server ID and project ID. |
| User | Server-local ID, name, email and local/OIDC identity; exactly one effective server role. Explicit project admission is separate from that role. |
| Agent | Server-local ID and owner user; explicit memberships can admit the agent to multiple projects. Each operation uses one authorized project context. |
| External source scope | Existing provider/host/tenant/resource identity, distinct from an ADHD project; a canonical claim names its owning server/project pair. |
| Project data/job | Explicit project ID plus existing actor/resource identity; no ownership inferred from an ID prefix, display label, browser selection or model output. |

Keep Admin, Developer and Viewer as server-wide roles. Admin retains full access
to every project. The proposed admission model adds an Admin-managed set of
projects for non-Admin users without introducing project roles: Developer keeps
the existing ability to create agents only on their own behalf, within admitted
projects; Viewer stays read-only. An agent's grants cannot exceed its owner's
current admission. Admin may manage agents for any owner. Only Admin grants
project access; Developer cannot admit themselves by creating an agent.

Keep existing local admin bootstrap/recovery and OIDC group-to-highest-server-role
rules. OIDC login does not automatically admit a new account to every project.
Specify any default admission explicitly; default to no project admission for new
non-Admin accounts. Migration admits existing users/agents to the legacy project
so upgrading preserves their prior access. Changes to membership, account status
and effective role must apply live to sessions, credentials and background work.
Equal emails across peers may correlate identity but never transfer roles,
admission, agent ownership or credentials.

Default coordination is project-local. A multi-project agent publishes,
subscribes, sends, polls and acknowledges in an explicitly selected project;
membership in two projects does not bridge their private messages or subscriptions.
Project event subscriptions are unfiltered by default in the target architecture;
an optional plain-text model filter narrows an authorized stream. Models are not
required for raw pub/sub or literal backend search. See KAFKA-001 through
KAFKA-009 for durable broker handoff, A2A acknowledgements and deployment scope.
Explicit multi-project discovery/query fan-out may search only admitted projects,
using separate project evidence and coverage. It does not implicitly publish a
result into another project. No automatic cross-project subscription matching is
included in the first implementation; agents may subscribe separately per project.

Project creation, rename, admission changes, archive and resume are hot Admin
operations. Archive must preserve originals and define the disposition of accepted
work, existing deliveries and canonical claims; it must not silently delete data.
Hard deletion, project transfer between servers and high-availability replication
are outside this first program and require separately specified policies.

MULTI-001 must classify every operation and configuration field before generation.
Use this minimum matrix and enumerate exact fields/operations in the contracts:
| Surface | Required scope or decision |
| Users, local passwords, OIDC, role/group policy, sessions | Server-wide; project admission checked independently on every authorized operation. |
| Agent credentials and owners | Server identity with explicit project grants; possession of a token never validates a requested project by itself. |
| Publish, get, search, source-event deduplication | Project; same source/item IDs in different projects cannot collide. |
| Direct messages, subscriptions, deliveries, acknowledgement | Project and actor; membership in another project never consumes these records. |
| Context/referents, corrections, citations, snapshots | Project; validate every reference, page token and transitive traversal. |
| History, retrieval, archive and federation queries | Project and owner; freeze explicit fan-out scope, budgets and policy revisions. |
| Feedback, cohorts, replay, recipes, indexes and optimizer selection | Project; shared code/model resources do not imply shared training or selection state. |
| Idempotency, sequence namespaces, cursors, caches and retries | Bind project and actor; cross-project reuse must never retrieve another project's result. |
| Catalogs, canonical source claims and export allowlists | Project-qualified evidence and export authorization, with server-wide conflict detection. |
| Listener, public URL, configuration location, global model capacity | Server-wide; configuration location remains the sole restart exception. |
| Matcher/retrieval policies, budgets and project descriptions | Explicit project overrides of declared server defaults; document inheritance/reset and effects on accepted work. |
| Peer authentication and trust | Server-wide transport identity plus explicit allowed origin/destination projects and export policy. |
| Health, status, audit and metrics | Minimal public server health; authorized server totals and project details without leaking hidden project existence. |

Authorization must happen before pagination, counts, cached-result reuse and model
request construction. Recheck authorization and export policy before committing
or returning asynchronous results. Hidden/unknown project and resource errors
must have a documented, consistent disclosure policy. Audit access changes and
operations using stable server/project/actor identities without recording secrets.
| Work item | Deliverable | Prerequisites |
| MULTI-001 | Identity, access and lifecycle contracts; full scope matrix; exact compatibility/wire design. | First action: inventory and author contracts. |
| MULTI-002 | Durable project registry, complete state partitioning and recoverable legacy migration. | MULTI-001, KAFKA-001 |
| MULTI-003 | User admission and agent memberships with server-side, live authorization. | MULTI-001, MULTI-002 |
| MULTI-004 | Project-scoped coordination and evidence pipelines; explicit local query fan-out. | MULTI-002, MULTI-003, KAFKA-001 |
| MULTI-005 | Multi-project catalogs, peer trust and asynchronous canonical routing. | MULTI-001, MULTI-003, MULTI-004 |
| MULTI-006 | Project-aware hot Admin forms, project selector and server/project settings. | MULTI-002 through MULTI-005 |
| MULTI-007 | Fair shared workers, budgets, lifecycle fencing, diagnostics and recovery. | MULTI-002, MULTI-004, MULTI-005 |
| MULTI-008 | Native/Docker qualification, protocol conformance and upgrade/operator/client documentation. | MULTI-001 through MULTI-007, KAFKA-009 |

Author normative contracts before implementation; write independent acceptance
alongside each phase. The final phase integrates existing phase evidence and runs
the complete regression matrix rather than postponing isolation tests until last.
Each active-work entry carries its own unchecked subtasks and evidence gate.
Complete MULTI-001 identity design, then KAFKA-001 transport design, before the
shared persistence/workflow phases. Coordinate the legacy migration with
KAFKA-008 and require combined Kafka qualification before MULTI-008 closes.

Select and justify backend storage layout in MULTI-002, separating it from
Kafka event transport and coordinating outbox/cutover recovery. Preserve the current
DETS backend unless evidence requires a separately recorded change. Every key,
relationship, index manifest, cache and durable worker record must have a defined
project boundary regardless of whether storage is shared or separated per project.
Keep one writer per physical store and atomic acceptance/idempotency semantics.

Map the existing single-project configuration/store into one explicit default
project. Preserve its original project identity/aliases, server ID, user and agent
ownership, credentials, source identities, immutable originals, private deliveries,
acknowledgements, in-flight jobs and query results. Retain optimizer selections and
qualification provenance; where the new architecture invalidates qualification,
mark it stale and require requalification rather than claiming equivalence.

Provide preflight, schema versions, backup requirements and recoverable migration
markers. Concurrent startup, interruption, partial config/store commits and restore
collisions must fail closed. Reapplying migration is safe. Document when an older
binary cannot open the upgraded store and require restoring the matching backup
rather than promising an unsafe downgrade. Specify full-server and project-level
backup/restore, identity collisions and missing user/agent references explicitly.

Project identity cannot change through rename. Resolve the current configurable
`project_id` rename behavior with stable IDs and aliases, preserving old provenance
and retry behavior. Do not silently merge projects whose labels or aliases collide.

Before assigning new version numbers, classify each wire change for compatibility.
Continue agent communication over A2A; peer transport may remain HTTP. Publish
exact request/response/error schemas, state machines, bounds, version/capability
negotiation, canonicalization, request correlation and normative examples. Maintain
the rigorous existing unknown-field, framing and independently validated schema
requirements. A2A contextId and UI selection alone never authorize project access.

Permit legacy omission of project context only when the credential or negotiated
legacy endpoint is bound unambiguously to the migrated default project. Document
the exact rule; never choose the first project or infer one from user input.
Old project-bound peers must be mapped explicitly to their permitted project pair.
Reject unsupported or ambiguous interactions without silent downgrade or exposing
other local projects. Test both upgraded-to-old and old-to-upgraded directions.

Authenticate the peer server before trusting origin/destination project claims.
Authorize each pair against current grants. Bind durable request/status/results to
origin server, origin project, destination server/project, query ID and permitted
evidence. Preserve deadlines, cancellation, retries and duplicate suppression.
Shared endpoints must not let one remote project impersonate another or poll its
queries. Keep credentials, private messages and restricted context out of exports.

Catalog discovery lists only projects and source scopes approved for that peer.
Cache complete advertised catalogs by server/project/revision with freshness and
invalidation rules. Canonical ownership of an exact external scope names one
server/project pair; duplicates across projects on the same server are conflicts
just as duplicates across servers are. Copies never become canonical implicitly.
Route to a local canonical project without self-HTTP or relaxed authorization.
Fan-out results identify project, owner, evidence, coverage and unavailable scopes;
discovery never claims knowledge of all projects in the federation.

Use at least two populated projects on one server, a third inaccessible project,
two coordinating agents per populated project and one explicitly multi-project
agent. Deliberately reuse actor-local IDs, source IDs, message IDs, labels and
content across projects. Test each public operation and every indirect path for
cross-project reads, writes, deduplication and model-input leakage.

Use at least three real federated server processes, with multiple projects on
each, to test discovery, same-server and remote canonical ownership, conflicts,
mixed versions, export restrictions, stale caches, outages and bounded retries.
Verify asynchronous incremental results and accurate partial coverage.

Run actual legacy-store migrations and process-kill tests around migration,
configuration and worker commits. Exercise live access/OIDC changes, project
archive/resume, token rotation, browser switches and concurrent Admin revisions.
Saturate one project's matcher/query/optimizer and remote requests while another
continues within documented fairness bounds; retain real inference accounting.

Qualify the exact generated artifact and Docker image with independent SDK,
wire-validator, desktop/mobile browser and existing live Nemotron model evidence.
Run a model-free raw pub/sub and literal-search profile as well as optional
short-response filtering/search evidence. KAFKA-007 adds real Compose and
Kubernetes deployment qualification. Keep semantic subscription matching fast
and decisive. Record ordinary single-project
regressions alongside multi-project results. Close the program only when every
MULTI item has its required evidence; document remaining deployment/publication
gates separately and make no claims from old single-project qualification alone.

Pivot project event distribution to Apache Kafka. Each logical ADHD server has
its own Kafka service serving its local projects. Agents continue to communicate
with ADHD through A2A and need neither Kafka credentials nor a Kafka client.
A subscription may receive all authorized project events across all agents,
or narrow that stream using an optional plain-text Jev-like model filter.
Backend facts remain searchable independently of subscriptions. Models may support
semantic search and optional filtering; raw pub/sub must work without a model.

The combined implementation has an [initial lifecycle admission](../../verification/multi-eventing/lifecycle-admission-30.json).
The eventing contracts select the pinned Kafka REST Proxy adapter; the deployment
artifacts provide Compose and Kubernetes packaging. [Native eventing and federation
qualification](../verification/native-eventing.json) covers the current artifact.
Final program qualification remains open for the complete container, deployment,
recovery and regression matrix. Existing closed work retains its historical
evidence and cannot attest this architecture.

The pivot composes with [multiple projects per server](multi-project.md). Kafka
is per server, not per project or per agent. A Kafka service can be one development
broker or a replicated deployment; resilience claims depend on the selected
topology. Federation remains an authenticated ADHD-to-ADHD protocol. Private
brokers are not exposed to agents or peers, and broker mirroring is not selected
as a federation transport. Canonical ownership and export authorization still
apply before any remote information is disclosed. A future cross-server event
subscription bridge needs its own exact contract; this program does not silently
replicate every local project into peer brokers.

```mermaid
flowchart LR
    Agent[Agents] <-->|A2A| Hub[ADHD authorization and API]
    Hub --> Commit[Durable original and event handoff]
    Commit --> Backend[Searchable originals and indexes]
    Commit --> Kafka[This server's Kafka service]
    Kafka --> Select[Project and deterministic selectors]
    Select --> Raw[Unfiltered subscription]
    Select --> Filter[Optional plain-text model filter]
    Raw --> Delivery[Durable recipient deliveries]
    Filter --> Delivery
    Delivery -->|A2A poll and ack| Hub
```

This is a logical separation, not a claim that Kafka and the backend share a
transaction. KAFKA-001/002 must specify the authoritative commit point and durable
handoff, such as a backend transaction with an outbox and idempotent publication.
The backend retains originals; Kafka carries project events; ADHD retains
subscription identity, delivery/ack state and retry/deduplication authority.
| Mode | Meaning | Model requirement |
| Project stream | All project-published events, across all agents, including the subscriber's own publications. | None; no inference calls. |
| Deterministic selection | Optional explicit event type/source/publisher selectors within the admitted project. | None; ordinary exact selection. |
| Semantic filter | Plain-text criterion applied after project/metadata selection to narrow the stream. | Configured short-response decision adapter. |

Published project information is the initial event stream. Private addressed
messages, passwords, tokens, role changes and internal control records are not
project-public events. Direct messages retain their authorized A2A delivery path;
any broker use for them must have separately specified private storage and ACLs.
All events still require project admission, owner checks and current export policy.
A model chooses relevance, never permissions.

Subscription schemas must distinguish an absent filter from invalid/blank filter
text and preserve old described subscriptions as filtered mode. New unfiltered
subscriptions require no dummy description or model endpoint. For example, an
agent can subscribe to every event in project P, then optionally add “Only API
compatibility changes or blocked releases.” The exact wire fields belong to the
normative contract phase rather than this illustrative prose.

Define the activation watermark atomically relative to publication acceptance.
Preserve the existing default of new events only; historical replay is explicit,
bounded and authorized. Specify pause/resume and filter edits as revisions with
an exact effective watermark. Pending evaluations use a documented revision;
late decisions cannot silently apply a new predicate to an old job. Define
overlapping subscriptions using the existing one-logical-delivery-per-recipient
publication behavior where compatible, with subscription reasons/provenance.
Raw deliveries must not invent model scores, thresholds or model names.

If a model is absent, reject or explicitly pause new semantic-filter requests
with a documented state. If it fails after acceptance, preserve pending work and
expose retry/error status. Never turn an outage into a negative match or silently
drop the filter and disclose all events. Bound filter backlog/costs independently
so raw subscriptions and other projects continue making progress.

Kafka consumer-group load sharing is different from giving every subscriber its
own complete stream. Choose a bounded ADHD fan-out design with durable per-agent
subscription state; do not put unrelated agent subscribers into one shared worker
group and accidentally divide their events. Decide topic/group cardinality and
cleanup from project/subscription scale, rather than creating a topic per agent
by default.

Specify event ID, stable server/project identity, publisher/source provenance,
schema version, timestamps, topic key, partitioning and size bounds. Record the
ordering promise: partition ordering does not itself establish project-wide or
cross-project order. Preserve existing A2A delivery ordering where promised,
or document a reviewed versioned change. Define poison-message isolation,
retry limits, dead-letter review and authorized replay without treating a failed
record as successfully delivered.
Distinguish these durable positions explicitly:
1. Original accepted and retry identity committed.
2. Event handed off to Kafka with known durability settings.
3. Event materialized into subscription/filter work and recipient deliveries.
4. Backend/search projection caught up to an exposed watermark.
5. Recipient acknowledges a delivery through A2A.

Commit broker processing progress only after recoverable downstream work exists.
Broker progress is not the agent acknowledgement. Agent polls do not consume or
acknowledge records; repeat delivery remains possible. Define out-of-order/batch
acks without advancing a cursor past unacknowledged records. Process crashes,
rebalances and duplicate publications must retain one logical original/delivery
using stable IDs and deduplication, without claiming exactly-once network receipt.

Kafka transactions cover Kafka records and consumer offsets; external backend
writes and A2A receipts need their own coordination. This boundary follows
[Apache Kafka's delivery/transaction design](https://kafka.apache.org/41/design/design/).
That reference informs the plan; it is not a selected deployment version.

Broker retention must never silently discard accepted unacknowledged deliveries
or original facts. Specify durable delivery materialization/spooling and bounded
admission/backpressure for disconnected agents and long filter outages. If a
consumer loses retained offsets, expose an explicit gap and define recovery from
durable originals or an operator-controlled replay; never reset to latest and
claim complete delivery. Define time/size retention, compaction eligibility,
deduplication lifetime and restore behavior together.

Store originals/provenance regardless of subscription presence or filter outcome.
Kafka retention is an event-transport policy, not the fact-history retention
policy. Literal/metadata search and ID retrieval continue without a model.
Semantic retrieval, history/archive answers, replay and optimizer workflows can
use configured models, with explicit capability, unavailable/error and coverage
states. Their failure must not make basic eventing unavailable.

Define read-after-publish behavior and expose projection/index watermarks and lag.
A lagging index is not evidence that a fact does not exist. Preserve originals,
citations, corrections, authorization and project isolation during catch-up,
rebuild and replay. Pub/sub semantic filters are separate from search-time model
work and retain separate queues, budgets and metrics.

Provide hot, role-scoped Admin forms for broker connection/security references,
topic/retention policy, raw/filtered subscription modes, filter thresholds,
model enablement, backlog/lag, recovery and replay controls. Retain exactly one
server role plus MULTI project admission. Apply revisioned configuration with
consumer fencing, cutover watermarks and secret redaction. Connection changes
must not reset offsets or replay a whole topic implicitly.

Configuration-file location remains the only setting requiring a hub restart.
Kafka infrastructure may require broker/controller rollouts for broker-owned
static settings; document them separately and orchestrate them without requiring
a hub restart. Expose supported app-managed settings in Admin; arbitrary cluster
administration, image upgrades and volume provisioning belong to deployment
tooling rather than unrestricted shell or Kubernetes access from the hub.

Ship both a Docker Compose application and a Kubernetes application. Each includes
the hub, private Kafka/KRaft service, persistent broker and backend volumes,
secret handling, resource limits and health/ready probes. A model-free baseline
must boot successfully with no GPU; an optional model profile uses the existing
decision service or a configured endpoint. Select pinned broker/client artifacts,
licenses and supported compatibility ranges during implementation. Decide plain
manifests versus a maintained chart/operator explicitly. K8s packaging does not
authorize multiple hub replicas against the current single-writer store: retain
one replica until a separate concurrency/HA contract is qualified.

Document startup/shutdown dependency behavior, unavailable broker admission,
backpressure, metrics, backups, volume restore, replacement and broker upgrades.
Distinguish single-node development durability from replicated Kafka durability.
Test broker and hub recovery independently and in combination.

Coordinate one migration with MULTI-002: preserve prior project identity, users,
agent credentials, originals, descriptions/filters, pending model jobs, delivery
IDs and acknowledgements. Define outbox initialization and cutover watermarks
without replaying all historical originals into new subscriptions. Specify
migration order for current single-project and already multi-project stores,
backups of both durable domains, repeatable crash recovery and downgrade limits.
Old semantic subscriptions must not silently become unfiltered subscriptions.

1. **Contracts and infrastructure:** KAFKA-001/002/007 define the event and
   subscription schemas, durable handoff, broker integration and both deployment
   packages. Establish the model-free startup path first.

2. **Agent streams and optional filtering:** KAFKA-003/004 add independent A2A
   subscriptions, polling/acknowledgement and isolated semantic-filter work.
   Demonstrate all-agent project fan-out without inference before adding filters.

3. **Facts and administration:** KAFKA-005/006 preserve backend search and add hot
   Admin configuration, diagnostics and safe connection/filter changes. A rejected
   filter decision must never remove the original from searchable history.

4. **Upgrade and qualification:** KAFKA-008/009 prove migration, recovery and
   interoperability on the exact combined multi-project artifact in Compose and
   Kubernetes before closing the program.

The minimum end-to-end demonstration uses agents A and B publishing in project P
and two independent subscribers. One subscribes to every P event; the other adds
the plain-text criterion “API compatibility changes.” Both publishers' events
reach the raw subscriber with zero model calls; only matching events reach the
filtered subscriber. With the model disabled, raw delivery and literal fact search
continue. Filtered work reports its unavailable/pending state, and every accepted
original remains searchable, including events rejected by the filter. Events in
an unauthorized project remain inaccessible through every path.
| Item | Deliverable | Dependencies |
| KAFKA-001 | Contracts, dependency/client selection, event/subscription modes and durability design. | MULTI-001 |
| KAFKA-002 | Per-server Kafka, event publication and recoverable backend handoff. | KAFKA-001, MULTI-002 |
| KAFKA-003 | Independent subscriber fan-out and A2A delivery/ack bridge. | KAFKA-002, MULTI-003, MULTI-004 |
| KAFKA-004 | Optional semantic filters with isolated failure/revision handling. | KAFKA-003 |
| KAFKA-005 | Durable backend fact search and model-independent eventing. | KAFKA-002, MULTI-004 |
| KAFKA-006 | Hot Admin controls, broker/filter diagnostics and access. | KAFKA-003 through KAFKA-005, MULTI-006 |
| KAFKA-007 | Compose and Kubernetes applications with optional model profile. | KAFKA-002 |
| KAFKA-008 | Coordinated migration and cutover/recovery. | KAFKA-003 through KAFKA-005, KAFKA-007 |
| KAFKA-009 | Integrated independent qualification and documentation. | KAFKA-001 through KAFKA-008, MULTI-007 |

MULTI-002 and MULTI-004 consume KAFKA-001's design. MULTI-008 additionally waits
for KAFKA-009. This gives one combined release target without making contract
work depend on final qualification. Keep each work item's acceptance alongside
implementation; do not postpone all fault/privacy tests until the last phase.

Qualification must include real Kafka, multiple projects, several independent
subscribers and publishers, unauthorized projects, overlapping subscriptions,
offline agents, model absence/failure, broker outages/rebalances, expired offsets,
outbox/projection faults and crash injection at durable handoffs. Prove zero
inference for raw subscriptions and functioning basic fact search in Compose and
Kubernetes with no model. Separately qualify live-model semantic filters/search.
Run A2A SDK and independently validated wire traffic, desktop/mobile Admin flows,
legacy migrations, federation using separate per-server brokers and fair scheduling
at documented limits. Bind evidence to exact generated artifact, container,
broker/client and deployment identities before closing any gate.

owner_label_limitation: Prior inventory ownerlabels are provenance/routing heuristics; exact requirement text and current scoped evidence determine qualification, not an inferred new dependency from a label.
